findings.note: The judge override is folded into the run vars unconditionally, so an ambient METAREVIEW_JUDGE_MODEL (or METAREVIEW_JUDGE_EFFORT) makes every `fsm init --calibration` fail: applyJudgeOverride puts JUDGE into the vars map and workflow.Resolve refuses any caller-supplied JUDGE under calibration with ERR_CALIBRATION_PINNED. run.go only translates CodeVarUnset, so the operator sees a raw pinned-var error with no hint that an environment variable, not a flag, caused it, and no way to run calibration without unsetting the env. Spec 3 section 2 step 3 applies exactly this protection on the fork path (strip JUDGE/JUDGE_EFFORT before Resolve for a calibration parent); the init path has no equivalent. The same unconditional injection turns --judge-model on a workflow that does not declare JUDGE into `ERR_VAR_UNKNOWN: unknown var JUDGE`. The new test file in this shard is the whole test surface for this feature and covers neither case.

findings.note: The spec contradicts itself on the DiffRuns common-prefix tuple. The r4 header says `CommonPrefixSeq` over (Type, Node, Data), the r5 header says the tuple includes `Origin` presence, and section 4 says (Type, Node, At, Data) with Origin, Seq and Prev explicitly ignored. Only section 4 matches the shipped code and the F7 test row: if Origin presence were part of the tuple, a fork of a root parent would always yield 1 (the parent's events carry no Origin, the child's copies do), contradicting the F7 assertion CommonPrefixSeq == ForkedAtSeq. The two header lines are stale and should be corrected or dropped so an implementer reading the changelog does not get the wrong rule.

evidence.note: r5 header: CommonPrefixSeq tuple includes Origin presence
section 4: identical (Type, Node, At, Data); Origin, Seq and Prev are ignored
the implementation compares Type, Node, At and Data only

findings.note: Two small spec-to-code drifts in the section 5 / section 4 type listings: Manifest.Bytes is documented as the sum of all written files, while the implementation documents and computes it as every written file except manifest.json itself; and Report.Outcomes is declared [2]run.Outcome in the spec but is [2]string in the shipped type. Both are documentation-accuracy defects, not behaviour defects.

findings.note: TestRealCodexExec pins the three exit paths but not stderr, and realCodexExec never assigns cmd.Stderr: on the 'ran and failed' path the child's stderr is discarded, so a Codex CLI that fails with an empty stdout hands the judge an empty answer and a bare exit code with no diagnostic anywhere. Capturing stderr (even truncated, into the returned error or a warn) would make the failure legible; the test file is the natural place to pin it.
